segments.he: עַל יְדֵי הַצְּעָקָה אֶל ה' מֵעמֶק הַלֵּב יָכוֹל לָשׁוּב אַף עַל
segments.en: This is the essential rectification Yaakov established — that even in the depth of the darkness of the exile we seek and search for Hashem with powerful desires, even when it seems one cannot find, in the aspect of "I sought him but did not find him." Even so: "I will rise and roam through the city, through the streets and the squares" [Shir HaShirim 3:2] — this is the heart of what Yaakov established: that in the depth of the darkness we seek and search for Hashem with intense longing, until through this one will spontaneously gather strength to open one's mouth in words of prayer. For truly this is the essence of perfect prayer always. And this is the meaning of: "Do not make your prayer fixed" — for prayer must emerge from genuine desire and longing. Yet one must also establish obligatory prayers for the sake of the masses, without which they would not pray at all. But Yaakov, who lowered himself all the way to the very end — to the ikves Meshicha [footsteps of Moshiach] — established the essential rectification: that Maariv is voluntary, so that even in the depth of darkness one strengthens oneself with powerful desires, until one spontaneously awakens to pray willingly. This is the ultimate rectification of prayer.

segments.he: בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ אֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר שֶׁיַּעֲמד בִּפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתוּב כָּל בָּאֶיהָ לא יְשׁוּבוּן וְכוּ' וְאִיתָא בַּזּהַר שֶׁאֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה עַל פְּגַם טִפֵּי הַמּחַ אַף עַל פִּי כֵן בֶּאֱמֶת מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה וְכַמּוּבָא בְּכָל סִפְרֵי מוּסָר, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי מִפִּי רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בְּפֵרוּשׁ, רַק מֵחֲמַת שֶׁפָּגַם כָּל כָּךְ עַל כֵּן הוּא צָרִיךְ לְהִתְנַסּוֹת וּלְהִצְטָרֵף וְלַעֲמד בַּנִּסָּיוֹן הַזֶּה שֶׁל הִתְרַחֲקוּת הַזּאת, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁיַּרְחִיקוּ אוֹתוֹ כָּל כָּךְ בְּכָל מִינֵי הִתְרַחֲקוּת, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁכּוֹתְבִין עָלָיו שֶׁאֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה וְכוּ'.
segments.en: Although the baal teshuvah [one engaged in return] must cry out and weep greatly before Hashem and greatly break his heart — as it is written: "A broken and crushed heart, O G-d, You will not despise" [Tehillim 51:19] — nonetheless he must also be expert in the halachah, so that this does not distance him from Hashem more than before. For in every path of holiness there is the aspect of: "The righteous walk in them, while sinners stumble in them" [Hoshaya 14:10] — the aspect of "if one merits it, it becomes a life-giving potion; if not..." The baal teshuvah must certainly bear humiliations and self-effacement in various forms. The essential teshuvah is to be silent and still when one hears one's own shame, and to fulfill "Be still before Hashem." This includes also bearing the humiliations one inflicts upon oneself — in the aspect of "shame has broken my heart" [Tehillim 69:21] — for one must feel shame before oneself for one's sins and failings, until one's blood rushes inward. As our Sages taught: "Whoever transgresses and is ashamed of it is forgiven for all his sins." Yet even so, one must be highly expert in this halachah not to descend from it into sadness and melancholy of the Sitra Achra. As our Master warned and said: "A broken heart is a different matter from sadness — one must guard carefully that sadness not take hold from the broken heart." He therefore commanded to strengthen oneself to be in joy throughout the day through all the ways of his holy counsel — only at a specific time to have a broken heart, to pour out one's speech before Him as a son before his father. And all this is contained in the concept of expertise in the halachah described above.

segments.he: וּכְשֶׁהוּא פֶּתִי וְסָכָל וְאֵינוֹ מְרַחֵם עַל עַצְמוֹ שֶׁלּא לְאַבֵּד אֶת עוֹלָמוֹ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אֲזַי מוֹצֵא פְּטוּר לְעַצְמוֹ לְהִתְרַחֵק מִן הַתְּשׁוּבָה מֵאַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר נִכְתַּב עָלָיו שֶׁאֵין מוֹעִיל לוֹ תְּשׁוּבָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אֲבָל מִי שֶׁחוֹשֵׁב בֶּאֱמֶת עַל הַתַּכְלִית שֶׁלּוֹ וְיֵשׁ לוֹ רַחֲמָנוּת עַל עַצְמוֹ, אֲזַי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרוֹאֶה כָּל מִינֵי הִתְרַחֲקוּת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתוּב עָלָיו שֶׁאֵין מוֹעִיל לוֹ תְּשׁוּבָה אַף עַל פִּי כֵן אֵין מִסְתַּכֵּל עַל זֶה כְּלָל, אַדְּרַבָּא יֵשׁ לוֹ רַחֲמָנוּת יוֹתֵר עַל עַצְמוֹ כִּי אַף עַל פִּי כֵן מַה יְּהֵא בְּסוֹפוֹ וּמַה יַּעֲשֶׂה לְיוֹם פְּקֻדָּה, וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לְהַטְעוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ שֶׁלּא לְאַבֵּד אֶת עוֹלָמוֹ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כָּל מַה שֶּׁמּוֹצֵא וְרוֹאֶה שֶׁמְּרַחֲקִין אוֹתוֹ יוֹתֵר, הוּא מְרַחֵם עַל עַצְמוֹ יוֹתֵר, וְצוֹעֵק אֶל ה' יוֹתֵר וְיוֹתֵר מֵעֻמְקָא דְּלִבָּא, עַד יַשְׁקִיף וְיֵרֶא ה' מִשָּׁמַיִם, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ חָפֵץ חֶסֶד הוּא, וְאֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר שֶׁיַּעֲמד בִּפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ כְּבָר בְּכַמָּה וְכַמָּה רְשָׁעִים גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁפָּגְמוּ בְּטִפֵּי הַמּחַ וְכָפְרוּ בָּעִקָּר וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן נִתְקַבְּלוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה, וַאֲזַי כְּשֶׁזּוֹכֶה לַעֲמד בַּנִּסָּיוֹן הַזֶּה וְשָׁב בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵמָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּדְמֶה לוֹ שֶׁמַּרְחִיקִין אוֹתוֹ כַּנַּ"ל, אֲזַי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מְרַחֵם עָלָיו וְנִתְקָרֵב עַל יְדֵי זֶה דַּיְקָא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁעָמַד בְּנִסָּיוֹן זֶה שֶׁל הִתְרַחֲקוּת כַּנַּ"ל וְהָבֵן. (הִלְכוֹת תְּפִלִּין הֲלָכָה ג אוֹת ד):
segments.en: This is the aspect of the four species taken in the hands [on Sukkos]. The holy Zohar states: "Who has prevailed? The one who holds the weapon of war in his hand." At first glance this seems to make no sense. In all wars, who has prevailed? The one who has subdued the battle, overpowered, thrown down, and killed the enemy. And the answer given — "the one who holds the weapon of war in his hand" — on the contrary: in every war, this is a sign that one has not yet won, since one still needs to hold the weapons. One who has truly won the battle no longer needs to hold weapons!
